newsitem.title: USA: Clinton briefs lawmakers on Iraq strategy.
newsitem.headline: Clinton briefs lawmakers on Iraq strategy.

text.p: President Bill Clinton briefed key members of Congress on Tuesday on his strategy for restraining Iraqi military activity amid signs of a holding action on new U.S. muscle-flexing in the Gulf.

Clinton met Republican and Democratic leaders of the Senate and House of Representatives and the chairmen and ranking members of relevant congressional committees in the state dining room of the White House, White House spokeswoman Mary Ellen Glynn said.

Glynn said the meeting was expected to last about an hour and that it was informational in nature. It was the first time Clinton had met with the lawmakers since he ordered two cruise missile strikes on Iraqi air defence installations and widened a no-fly zone in southern Iraq.
Those actions came in response to Iraqi attacks on one of the factions involved in Kurdish infighting in northern Iraq.

Joining Clinton in the briefing were Secretary of State Warren Christopher and Defence Secretary William Perry, who was just back from trying to rally support for U.S. policy toward Iraq among allied nations in the Middle East.

Several hours before the meeting started, a U.S. military spokesman in Kuwait said that plans to reinforce U.S. troops in the tiny Gulf emirate were on standby. Kuwait was invaded by Iraqi forces in 1990, touching off the 1991 Gulf War.
